articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy 2026 Odds as Arch Manning and Jeremiah Smith Rise, Dante Moore Falls
articles.summary: The early 2026 Heisman Trophy race gained some more clarity as Saturday's action unfolded.
articles.body:
The early 2026 Heisman Trophy race gained some more clarity as Saturday's action unfolded.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning's Heisman Trophy odds improved to +2500 following the team's 24-23 win over Ohio State, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith's Heisman odds moved to +440 despite the loss.

Oregon quarterback Dante Moore's Heisman odds fell to +4000 after the No. 6 Ducks suffered a 39-31 upset loss against Oklahoma State.

Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton also saw his Heisman Trophy odds move to +2200 with the Bulldogs' 70-20 blowout win over Western Kentucky, via FanDuel Sportsbook. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr owns +1000 Heisman Trophy odds following a lopsided victory over Rice as well.

Manning finished 23-of-37 for 196 yards and one touchdown compared to one interception as the Longhorns came back from a 20-point deficit to emerge victorious.

Smith still shined in the defeat, catching eight passes for 164 yards and one score.

Carr thrived against Rice, finishing 16-of-20 for 253 yards and four touchdowns without tossing an interception. His performance was particularly impressive considering he was replaced by backup quarterback Noah Grubbs midway through the third quarter.

Moore went 14-of-29 for 191 yards and two touchdowns without getting picked off against Oklahoma State, but it wasn't enough for his team to emerge victorious.

It was a particularly disappointing result considering the Cowboys entered the contest on a 12-game losing streak, which included a loss to Tulsa in which they allowed 361 total yards to open their 2026 campaign.

As for Stockon, he threw for 234 yards and five touchdowns while completing 81.3 percent of his throws against Western Kentucky before he was taken out in the second quarter. He also averaged 14.6 yards per attempt.

Georgia improved to 2-0 with the victory.

articles.title: Arteta seethes at Sunderland penalty decision despite Arsenal win
articles.summary: Arsenal maintain perfect start to the season with their fourth win, thanks to goals from Guimaraes and Saka.
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel ‌Arteta has labelled the decision to award Sunderland a penalty ‘unacceptable’ after watching his side ⁠grind out a 2-0 ⁠win to maintain their 100 percent start to the season and move clear at the top of the Premier League.

The defending champions made ⁠it 12 points out of 12 on Saturday as David Raya’s penalty save in the 55th minute proved crucial for the visitors, who went ahead two minutes later ⁠with Bruno Guimaraes’s first goal for the club.

Bukayo Saka wrapped it up deep in stoppage time from the penalty spot to ⁠make it four league wins out of four for the reigning champions.

It could have been different had Enzo Le Fee found the net, but Arteta blasted the decision by referee John Brooks to award a penalty when Ezri Konsa was penalised for pulling down Dan Ballard as a corner was played in.

“It was a huge win ‌, but it could have been something very different,” an angry Arteta said when referring to the penalty award after the match.

“It’s unacceptable at this level; this can change the course of a season and the championship. It’s not acceptable. I’ve seen it 10 times to make sure, and it’s not possible at this level that it can be a penalty. It cannot happen.

“It’s not a penalty in any context, in any league.”

It was far from a vintage Arsenal display against a tenacious Sunderland, who ⁠deserved something for their endeavour, but they dug deep and showed the resilience ⁠that helped them win a first title for 22 years last season.

They have now kept four clean sheets in their five games since the start of the season, including in the Champions League win at Napoli in midweek.

Summer signing Guimaraes replaced Myles ⁠Lewis-Skelly at half-time and made a stunning impact.

After receiving a pass from Declan Rice, he sent a right-footed curler into the top corner.

Arsenal were forced to ⁠defend desperately at times as Sunderland’s physicality rattled them, but ⁠Saka netted his third goal of the season when he beat Robin Roefs with his spot-kick after being fouled by Reinildo Mandava, who was sent off.

“It’s unbelievable the spirit and the courage we have to go again and again and again,” Arteta said. “So ‌pleased in one sense and so worried in another.

“David Raya was unbelievable. He is a player that decides football matches when we need it.

“Sunderland deserve a lot of credit for the way they make it ‌so ‌hard for you.”

Manchester City, the only other side not to have dropped Premier League points this season, can join Arsenal on 12 points if they beat Manchester United on Sunday.

articles.title: Arsenal reaction: 'Today the game was unprotected' - Arteta fumes but Gunners survive
articles.summary: Arsenal produced a gritty 2-0 win against Sunderland, but Mikel Arteta fumed about the penalty that could have cost his side a result.
articles.body:
Arsenal 's duality was there for all to see in their 2-0 win at Sunderland : gritty defence and moments of genius.

But things could have turned out very differently had a crucial 121-second period gone the other way.

After close to an hour of physical, full-blooded football, Sunderland were given a penalty when Ezri Konsa fouled Dan Ballard at a corner.

It proved the turning point - David Raya tipped Enzo le Fee's spot kick on to the post, and just over two minutes later, Arsenal substitute Bruno Guimaraes crashed in the opener off the underside of the crossbar.

Arteta's side left the north-east of England with their ninth successive Premier League victory. Not since the days of the Invincibles, in 2003-04, have the Gunners done that.

Yet Arteta was furious about the Sunderland penalty that could have cost his side.

"It's a judo roll from the opponent. Ezri [Konsa] does nothing. Just watch it," Arteta told BBC Match of the Day.

"We have a lot of cameras and VAR, we have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the game and the momentum which is a really, really serious thing."

Referee John Brooks took a few seconds to point to the penalty spot after Ballard and Konsa hit the ground, but once he did the VAR stuck with his decision.

Konsa was certainly committing a foul, though Ballard did appear to have a hold of the Arsenal man.

"This should never happen, it's not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense," said Arteta, who was booked in the first half for repeatedly leaving his technical area.

"I'm making it very clear publicly because it's for the game, it's not only for Arsenal , this cannot happen at this level.

"It's not acceptable, I've watched it 20 times and can't think of why it was given."

This season, Premier League referees have been instructed to clamp down on grappling at corners, something that became a big talking point last term.

"With the new laws trying to get rid of the grappling, Konsa is all over Ballard. You have to be looking at the ball," former England midfielder Karen Carney said on TNT Sports.

"Ballard was holding Konsa's arm but you run the risk," added former Arsenal defender Martin Keown.

"They want to stamp down on it so there is no point arguing about it."

However, Arteta was not alone in questioning the decision.

"It's absolutely not a penalty. He has got it completely wrong, Konsa's shoulder is pulled down by Ballard and he lands on top," former Wales defender Ashley Williams said on BBC Match of the Day.

"It's like a perfect toss in judo. It's very clever by Ballard but in no way is it a penalty."

'Magnificent' Raya and defence survive 'chaotic' moments

Though Arteta spoke more about the awarding of the penalty rather than Raya's saving of it, there is no denying that the Spanish goalkeeper's intervention changed the direction of the match.

The save - only Raya's second penalty stop in the Premier League - came at a time when Sunderland were putting the defending champions under pressure.

Though Le Fee telegraphed his effort, Raya had to be at full stretch to tip it on to the post. Until that point, the goalkeeper had largely been a spectator.

"He keeps us alive in the game, that unbelievable moment saving the penalty," Guimaraes told TNT Sports.

"I think after this moment we [took from it] a big confidence to play forward and score our goal."

"This penalty save is exceptional. He gets out so quick," former Brentford manager Thomas Frank - the man who signed Raya - said on BBC Match of the Day.

"For me he's the best goalkeeper in the Premier League and one of the best in the world."

After building last season's title-winning campaign on a stubborn defence, the Gunners have begun this season with five clean sheets in six matches in all competitions, including in all three away matches.

"It is a fantastic win and the ground work was done by the defence. They have weathered the storm and the goalkeeper steps up and makes a wonderful save," Keown said.

"He is very important to Arsenal and what they achieve. He was magnificent and doesn't get the credit he deserves."

Though seething about the penalty, Arteta took the opportunity during his post-match media conference to praise his side's defensive efforts.

"We knew we would have to go through some difficult and chaotic moments to have the right to win this game," he said. "But we have done it."

Arsenal's brilliance at both ends helps overcome Sunderland

On a night when Arsenal were not at their fluid best, one hero was not going to be enough.

Guimaraes stepped up with a goal of the season contender, a curling effort from the edge of the penalty area.

The Brazilian midfielder has had a tough start to life at Arsenal since his £75m summer move from Newcastle , failing to start a match since the Community Shield.

Now recovered from a minor hamstring injury, he showed exactly what he can offer.

"That goal is about personality and character. It was him saying: I am going to make my mark at this football club," Keown said.

"He has been watching on the sidelines, but has said: 'Take a look at me - this is what I can do.'

"Boy did he shut the crowd up. A class player, going to the next level."

Of all the teams to announce himself against, Guimaraes chose the arch-rivals of his former employers Newcastle .

"It was a beautiful goal. Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle ," Guimaraes told TNT Sports.

"But now I'm trying to create a new history here and I start with the right foot."

This match could have turned out very differently for Arsenal , but in the end, it was heroes old and new that got the job done.

articles.title: El incombustible Natalio marca el camino del triunfo
articles.standfirst: Dos tantos del capitán, uno desde el centro del campo, y otro de Cris Montes, obran la remontada ante Unionistas
articles.summary: Dos tantos del capitán, uno desde el centro del campo, y otro de Cris Montes, obran la remontada ante Unionistas
articles.body: El Real Avilés firmó su primera gran tarde de la temporada con una remontada de autoridad frente al Unionistas de Salamanca CF (3-1), en un partido que empezó cuesta arriba para los locales y terminó siendo un ejercicio de contundencia en la segunda mitad. El capitán Natalio Poquet, con un doblete, y Cristian Montes, decisivo tras el descanso, dieron la vuelta a un choque que los charros habían abierto a su favor en apenas cuatro minutos. FICHA TÉCNICA Avilés: Álvaro Ratón; Aldai, Sillero, Mángel, Osky (Yago, m. 86); Mayo (Neskes, m. 83), Brais, Natalio (Mahicas, m. 76); Cris Montes (Pitu Doncel, m. 76), Cayarga (Lidueña, m. 83) y Santamaría. Unionistas; Daza; Morer (Saidi, m. 71), Serrano, Multiva, Retu; Marcelo (Arnau, m. 57), Álex Gil (Juanma, m. 57), Luis Alcalde; Álvaro Gómez, De Bustos (Willy, m. 79) y Pau Ferrer (De la Nava, m. 71). Goles 0-1: min. 4, De Bustos. 1-1: min. 40, Natalio. 2-1: min. 56, Cris Montes. 3-1: min. 61, Natalio. Árbitro Jesús López (Comité Gallego). Amonestó a Natalio y Samu Mayo; y a Álex Gil, Marcelo y Álvaro Gómez. Incidencias partido disputado en el estadio Román Suárez Puerta ante 3.102 espectadores. Un arranque de pesadilla y una reacción medida El guion no pudo comenzar peor para el conjunto asturiano. En el minuto 4, Hugo De Bustos aprovechó la primera oportunidad clara del encuentro para adelantar al Unionistas (0-1) y silenciar la afición local. El gol tempranero obligó al Avilés a reordenar ideas y a asumir el peso del partido durante una primera parte en la que el guardameta visitante Álex Daza fue protagonista. El correctivo llegó en el momento justo. En el minuto 40, Natalio Poquet igualó la contienda (1-1) para enviar a los equipos al descanso con todo por decidir. El empate premió la insistencia local y cambió por completo la dinámica anímica del duelo, que hasta entonces había vivido más de la tensión —cinco amonestaciones antes del intermedio, con Poquet, Álex Gil, Pau Ferrer y Alejandro Marcelo entre los amonestados— que del fútbol. Berto Cayarga enciende la remontada Si la primera mitad fue de tanteo, la segunda tuvo un dueño claro. El Real Avilés salió con otra intención y en el minuto 56 completó el vuelco: Cristian Montes, tras una asistencia de Berto Cayarga, puso el 2-1 y adelantó por primera vez a los suyos en el marcador. El extremo, incansable por la banda, volvió a aparecer seis minutos después: en el 62, su segundo pase de gol de la tarde encontró de nuevo a Natalio Poquet, que firmó el 3-1 definitivo y cerró su cuenta particular con un doblete de capitán. Con dos asistencias en apenas seis minutos, Cayarga fue el hombre que rompió el partido. El técnico local pudo administrar la ventaja en el tramo final, dando entrada a Roberto Doncel, Julián Mahicas, Alex Neskes, Daniel Lidueña y Yago Rodríguez para refrescar las piernas y proteger un resultado que ya no se le escapó. Los números del vuelco El 3-1 refleja bien la película: el Unionistas mandó pronto, pero no supo sostener su ventaja y acabó desbordado tras el intermedio. Los cambios visitantes —Arnau Casas, Juanma Lendínez, Abderrezzek Saidi, Carlos de la Nava y Willy Chatiliez— no alteraron la inercia de un encuentro que se les fue en cuestión de minutos. Álvaro Ratón mantuvo su portería a salvo tras el gol inicial, y el Avilés, dispuesto en un 4-4-2, encontró en la segunda parte la fluidez que le había faltado en la primera. Lo que dice la clasificación La victoria coloca al Real Avilés con 3 puntos en el Grupo 1, fruto de un balance de 1 victoria, 0 empates y 2 derrotas en tres jornadas, situándose en la duodécima posición con un saldo de goles equilibrado (4 a favor, 4 en contra). Es un primer respiro para un equipo que necesitaba sumar de tres tras un inicio irregular. Muy distinta es la situación del Unionistas de Salamanca CF. La derrota deja a los charros como colistas virtuales de la parte baja: 0 puntos, tres derrotas en tres partidos y un preocupante registro de 4 goles a favor por 10 en contra, el peor apartado defensivo del grupo. Solo la Unión Deportiva Ourense comparte con ellos la casilla sin puntuar. La imagen ofensiva del arranque en Avilés —ese gol de De Bustos a los cuatro minutos— contrasta con una fragilidad atrás que ya empieza a pesar en la tabla. En lo alto del grupo, el UD Logroñés manda con paso perfecto (9 puntos de 9 posibles), seguido del Athletic Club B U21 (7) y de un Real Unión Club que, con dos triunfos en dos partidos, suma 6 puntos y aún guarda un encuentro pendiente. El pelotón de perseguidores está apretado, y jornadas como esta empiezan a dibujar la frontera entre quienes aspiran a la zona alta y quienes deberán pelear por salir del pozo. Jugadores para seguir El foco del Avilés apunta directamente a Natalio Poquet. El capitán resolvió el partido con un doblete y demostró que su instinto sigue intacto en los metros finales; su gol del empate justo antes del descanso fue el punto de inflexión de la tarde. A su lado, Berto Cayarga se erigió en el gran arquitecto de la remontada: dos asistencias en la segunda mitad, ambas convertidas en gol, bastaron para desnivelar el choque. En el Unionistas, Hugo De Bustos dejó al menos un motivo para el optimismo con su tanto madrugador, un recurso ofensivo al que aferrarse mientras el equipo busca corregir sus problemas defensivos. Conclusión El Real Avilés se reencuentra con la victoria a base de carácter y de dos futbolistas en estado de gracia, mientras que el Unionistas de Salamanca CF se hunde en la última jornada del arranque liguero sin haber sumado todavía. Para los asturianos, un impulso necesario; para los charros, una señal de alarma que exige respuesta inmediata antes de que el foso se haga demasiado profundo.

articles.title: El Ourense deja unas sensaciones preocupantes
articles.standfirst: El triplete de Anai coloca a la UD Logroñés como líder provisional
articles.summary: El triplete de Anai coloca a la UD Logroñés como líder provisional
articles.body: El UD Logroñés se instala en lo más alto del Grupo 1 con un recital de su '20', autor de los tres tantos, mientras la UD Ourense encaja su tercera derrota consecutiva sin marcar todavía un solo gol. Hay partidos que se resumen en un nombre propio. El de la tercera jornada del Grupo 1 de Primera Federación entre la Unión Deportiva Ourense y el UD Logroñés se escribe entero con las letras de Anai Morales. El centrocampista firmó los tres goles del 0-3 definitivo y, de paso, catapultó a los riojanos al liderato en solitario de la categoría con pleno de victorias. Para el Ourense, en cambio, la tarde solo confirmó un arranque de temporada para olvidar. FICHA TÉCNICA UD Ourense: Rielo (Vizoso, min. 60), Varo, Labrada, Puime (Roi Currás, min. 76), Noel (Irazu, min. 66), Champi, Rivelott, Bastida, Carro (Xabi Domínguez, min. 61), Ferreiro y Rufo (Jansonas, min. 61). UD Logroñes: Taliby, Camacho, Cabetas, Adrián, Maroto (Issman, min. 83), David Amigo (Asenjo, min. 60), Baselga (Berto, min. 69), Navarro, Zabala (Amigo, min. 60), Anai y Santana (Miguelete, min. 69). Goles: 0-1, minuto 4: Anai. 0-2, minuto 57: Anai. 0-3, minuto 97: Anai. Árbitro: Almar Velasco (Vasco). Expulsó por doble amarilla al visitante Adrián (min. 71). Amonestó a Champi (min. 10), Ferreiro (min. 62), Irazu (min. 75) por parte local. Incidencias: O Couto, 1.722 espectadores. Un guion sentenciado desde el minuto 5 El Logroñés no perdió el tiempo. En el minuto 5, Anai Morales adelantó a los visitantes con un tanto que, sin necesidad de asistencia, puso patas arriba los planes del anfitrión. El madrugón condicionó por completo el desarrollo: el Ourense se vio obligado a perseguir un partido que nunca llegó a controlar. La reacción local se topó una y otra vez con el orden del bloque riojano, dispuesto en un 4-4-2 sólido y compacto. El único sobresalto para los visitantes en la primera parte llegó en forma de amonestaciones —Champi vio la amarilla en el minuto 11 y Eduardo Cabetas la vería en el 42—, pero el marcador no se movió hasta el descanso, que se alcanzó con el 0-1 en el electrónico. Morales rompe la resistencia y el Ourense se queda con diez Nada más regresar de vestuarios, el partido se decantó del todo. En el minuto 59, David Amigo asistió a Anai Morales para el 0-2 que dejaba muy tocada a la escuadra local. El técnico ourensano movió el banquillo de inmediato —hasta cinco cambios entre los minutos 61 y 78, con la entrada de Manu Vizoso, Xabier Domínguez, Romualdas Jansonas, Igor Irazu y Roi Currás—, pero la dinámica ya era irreversible. Por si fuera poco, el desenlace se complicó también para los visitantes en el plano numérico… aunque sin coste alguno. En el minuto 72, Eduardo Cabetas vio la segunda amarilla y, con ella, la roja, dejando al Logroñés con diez jugadores para los últimos compases. La inferioridad, lejos de reactivar al Ourense, no cambió nada: fue el conjunto riojano el que tuvo la última palabra. En el minuto 90, Miguelete —que había entrado en el 70— sirvió el balón para que Anai Morales completara su hat-trick y estableciera el 0-3 definitivo. Tres goles, un solo autor y un mensaje inequívoco de autoridad. Un líder con pleno y un colista sin estrenarse El resultado tiene una lectura clarísima en la clasificación. El UD Logroñés cierra la tercera jornada como líder en solitario del Grupo 1 con 9 puntos, fruto de tres victorias en tres partidos, 7 goles a favor y 2 en contra. Los riojanos se colocan por delante del Athletic Club B U21 (7 puntos) y de un Real Unión Club que suma 6 con un partido menos. En el extremo opuesto de la tabla se hunde la Unión Deportiva Ourense. El cuadro local ocupa la vigésima y última plaza del grupo con 0 puntos, tres derrotas en tres jornadas y un preocupante balance goleador: 0 tantos marcados y 6 encajados. Comparte los cero puntos con Unionistas de Salamanca CF (19º), pero por detrás en la diferencia de goles dentro del mismo saco de la parte más baja. Las claves de un duelo desigual El once inicial del Logroñés, comandado por su capitán Sergio Camacho en la línea defensiva y con la portería de Taliby Konate, mantuvo su meta a cero por segunda vez en el arranque liguero, algo que refrenda ese apartado defensivo de solo 2 goles encajados en tres jornadas. En el bando local, el capitán Champi y un David Ferreiro incansable en la medular intentaron dar continuidad al juego, pero la falta de acierto en el área rival vuelve a ser el gran lastre del proyecto ourensano: tres partidos, cero goles. La entrada del delantero lituano Romualdas Jansonas y del veterano Rufo desde el arranque no bastó para perforar una defensa que apenas concedió. El hombre del partido No hay debate posible. Anai Morales, dorsal 20 del Logroñés, firmó una actuación redonda: tres goles repartidos en los minutos 5, 59 y 90, uno en cada momento clave del encuentro —el que abrió la lata, el que la sentenció y el que puso la guinda—. Con contribuciones de David Amigo y Miguelete en las asistencias, el mediapunta se erige como la gran referencia ofensiva del líder. Lo que viene El Logroñés afronta el resto del curso con la moral por las nubes y la vitola de único equipo con pleno de victorias en el Grupo 1. La solidez atrás y la pegada de Morales dibujan a un candidato serio a pelear por los puestos de arriba. El Ourense, en cambio, tiene por delante una reconstrucción anímica urgente. Sumar el primer punto —y, sobre todo, marcar el primer gol— se ha convertido en la prioridad absoluta de un equipo que, de momento, cierra la clasificación sin haber inquietado apenas a sus rivales. La reacción tendrá que llegar pronto si no quiere que el arranque se convierta en un pozo del que sea difícil salir.

articles.title: Oregon's Shocking Loss to Oklahoma State Puts National Championship Hopes in Danger
articles.summary: On paper, it all made so much sense.
articles.body:
A dominant quarterback with true Heisman aspirations. Future NFL draft picks scattered across the defensive line. A stacked cupboard of elite wide receivers. Exceptional options up and down the roster—thanks largely to robust NIL budget—overflowing with speed and capable of swallowing college football whole.

Two weeks in, and Oregon's national championship aspirations are on life-support.

Sure, it's early. We can lean on that very obvious sentiment if you choose, and you wouldn't be wrong.

For a program that so many—including this writer—picked to win the national championship, it's hard to believe this is the conversation we're having in the middle of September.

But it's the conversation we must have after Oregon lost 39-31 against Oklahoma State.

Yes, that Oklahoma State. The team that won a grand total of one football game last year—the first one—before firing its head coach and completely rebooting. The team that plucked more than 60 players from the transfer portal and overhauled almost its entire roster with new faces. The team that lost outright to Tulsa as a double-digit favorite in Week 1.

Truth be told, the score should have been more lopsided. Oklahoma State should have beat Oregon, which began the season ranked No. 2 in the AP Poll, by at least two touchdowns if not more.

Oregon, which one assumed would have a dominant advantage on the line of scrimmage, struggled mightily in that department. The defense was gashed, and the offensive line never looked right.

With new coordinators on both sides of the ball, things look messy. That's putting it mildly.

Quarterback Dante Moore looked lost throughout much of the game, completing just 14 of 29 passes. The play calling was questionable; the execution was worse.

The total yards help tell the full story: Oklahoma State 554, Oregon 281.

For the Ducks, the issues don't stop with this loss. Those who wish to label this performance a "fluke" will have to address the performance against Boise State from Week 1 as well.

Dan Lanning's team gutted out a 34-27 victory last Saturday, although the optics were less than ideal. All the concerns that emerged on Saturday were evident one week ago.

All told, Oregon was favored by at least 24 points in its first two games. The Ducks will enter Week 3 having nearly lost both.

The good news, if there is any presently, is that the college football season doesn't end this week. Oregon has at least 10 more games to get right before the College Football Playoff doors close.

As we've seen in the past, it's much better to get the bad losses out of the way sooner than later. The selection committee has made this part obvious.

A lot can happen between now and then, and it's not farfetched to assume the team we saw fall flat on Saturday in Stillwater will at some point rebound.

Or perhaps what we witnessed on Saturday will persist throughout the year. Oregon could wind up being this year's Penn State—a team that garnered plenty of preseason national championship hype that year that fell flat on its face.

In less than two weeks, Oregon will play at USC. At this point, the Ducks are likely to be an underdog, starring a potential 2-2 start in the face.

The following game, the Ducks will take on a suddenly frisky UCLA. And later on, they'll play Ohio State in Columbus along with Michigan and Washington.

We can do the math. In recent history, teams with three losses don't make the College Football Playoff. That holds especially true for teams with bad losses on their resume, and this one certainly falls under that category presently.

This result will haunt this team, plain and simple.

Yes, it's early. But the full resume is building throughout. So, while it would be prudent to exercise patience and avoid any mammoth declarations, the situation is already dire.

And that's just the conversation to get into the College Football Playoff. Oregon has been there, done that.

This was a season that began with much greater aspirations than making the bracket. All the pieces were seemingly in place to do something more, and the expectations were drastically elevated as a result.

None of that matters now. Oregon must recalibrate, and it must do so quickly. The Ducks play Portland State in Week 3, and then, with the season seemingly on the brink, Oregon will travel to USC.

It's not too late to fix what suddenly feels like a broken season. But as the saying goes, it's getting late early.

articles.title: Unzueta, de penalti, dio la victoria al Mirandés en un duelo de locura
articles.standfirst: El conjunto de Fran Beltrán lo llegó a tener muy de cara: se adelantó 2-0, volvió a ponerse 3-2 y acabó cayendo tras jugar con diez desde el minuto 78 y encajar de penalti el 3-4 en el 93
articles.summary: El conjunto de Fran Beltrán lo llegó a tener muy de cara: se adelantó 2-0, volvió a ponerse 3-2 y acabó cayendo tras jugar con diez desde el minuto 78 y encajar de penalti el 3-4 en el 93
articles.body: Había de todo en el guion del Mérida AD ante el Mirandés, y todo terminó del lado visitante. Los extremeños tocaron el cielo con un 2-0 en la primera media hora, remontaron la remontada rival para volver a mandar 3-2 y, aun así, se marcharon con las manos vacías. El Mirandés, superior en pegada cuando el partido pedía sangre fría, firmó un 3-4 de infarto sellado por Iker Unzueta desde el punto de penalti en el minuto 90, con el Mérida ya reducido a diez. Un desenlace cruel para un anfitrión que jugó con fuego durante 90 minutos. FICHA TÉCNICA 3 - MÉRIDA: Csenterics; Jay, Nacho González, Fito Rodríguez, Hugo Sanz (Sandoval, min. 76); Martín Solar, Raúl Beneit, Javi Areso (Hugo Carrillo, min. 76), Darwin Guagua (Benny, min. 68), Jota López (Barbu, min. 87); Sofiane (Koné, min. 68). 4 - MIRANDÉS: Jesús Ruiz; Arrillaga (Pablo Pérez, min. 60), Peru Rodríguez, Arambarri, Aguirregabiria; Dela (Dorrio, min. 46), Raúl Martínez (Verde, min. 71), Markel Lozano (Julen, min. 84), Riki; Iker Unzueta y Uzkudun (Rodri Val, min. 71). GOLES: 1-0: Sofiane (min. 15). 2-0: Jay (min. 33). 2-1: Markel Lozano (min. 41). 2-2: Iker Unzueta (min. 43). 3-2: Jota (min. 75). 3-3: Julen (min. 85). 3-4: Unzueta, de penalti (min. 93). ÁRBITRO: Manuel Camacho (Comité Andaluz). Amonestó a los locales Hugo Sanz y Jota y a los visitantes Raúl Martínez. Expulsó con roja directa al local Martín Solar (min. 78). INCIDENCIAS: Partido de la tercera jornada de Primera Federación disputado en el Romano José Fouto ante 3.180 espectadores. Un arranque de ensueño para el Mérida El Estadio se rindió pronto a los locales. En el minuto 14, Sofiane El Ftouhi abrió la lata rematando un centro de Alejandro Jay para el 1-0. Y no fue una alegría aislada: en el 32, el propio Jay pasó de asistente a goleador tras un pase de Darwin Guagua —el activo más valioso del once local— para el 2-0. Con dos goles de renta y media hora por delante, el Mérida acariciaba una tarde redonda. Pero el fútbol rara vez perdona la complacencia. Justo cuando el marcador invitaba a soñar, el Mirandés reaccionó con una eficacia demoledora en apenas tres minutos. Markel Lozano recortó distancias en el 40 tras una asistencia de Hodei Arrillaga, y el mismo Arrillaga volvió a aparecer en el 43 para poner el 2-2 definitivo del descanso, esta vez habilitando a Iker Unzueta. Dos centros del lateral, dos goles: el Mirandés se fue al vestuario habiendo borrado en un suspiro toda la ventaja rival. Del sueño a la pesadilla en la segunda mitad Reanudado el choque, el Mérida no se escondió. En el minuto 75, Jota López —que ya había visto una amarilla en el 67— firmó de forma individual el 3-2 y devolvió la iniciativa a los locales. Parecía que la osadía extremeña iba a tener recompensa. El punto de inflexión llegó en el 83. Martín Solar vio la tarjeta roja directa y dejó a su equipo con diez hombres para el tramo decisivo, un desequilibrio numérico que el Mirandés no tardó en castigar. En el 87, el recién ingresado Julen —había entrado en el 85 por Peru Rodríguez— empató a tres tras asistencia de Riki. Y cuando el empate parecía el techo, un penalti en el 90 puso a Iker Unzueta ante su segunda diana de la noche. No falló: 3-4 y sentencia. Todavía hubo tiempo para las amarillas de Nacho González y Markel Lozano antes del pitido final. El doble filo de Iker Unzueta y los laterales del Mirandés El nombre de la jornada es Iker Unzueta. El delantero visitante firmó un doblete —su segundo tanto, el penalti del 90', valió los tres puntos— y se erige como la referencia ofensiva de un Mirandés que, cuando huele sangre, no perdona. Detrás de su pareja goleadora con Markel Lozano estuvo Hodei Arrillaga, autor de las dos asistencias que enderezaron el rumbo antes del descanso: un rendimiento de lateral que ataca como extremo. En el Mérida, la nota agridulce la puso Alejandro Jay, gol y asistencia desde la defensa, mientras que Darwin Guagua —el futbolista de mayor valor de mercado del once local— dejó su firma con el pase del segundo tanto. El talento estuvo; faltó el control emocional para gestionar dos ventajas. Lo que dice la clasificación El resultado remodela la zona media-alta del Grupo 1. El Mirandés escala hasta la quinta posición con 6 puntos (2 victorias, 1 derrota) tras tres jornadas, empatado con Pontevedra CF y a las puertas de los puestos de privilegio que encabeza un UD Logroñés con pleno de nueve puntos. El Mérida AD, en cambio, se hunde a la decimotercera plaza con 3 puntos (1 victoria, 2 derrotas) y un balance goleador de 4 a favor y 5 en contra. La sensación de haber merecido más contrasta con una realidad numérica preocupante: dos derrotas en tres salidas al ruedo y una fragilidad defensiva que ya ha costado puntos. Conclusión Fue un partido de esos que se recuerdan por su montaña rusa: 2-0, 2-2, 3-2 y 3-4. Ante 3.180 espectadores, el Mérida ofreció dos veces la mejor versión de sí mismo y dos veces se dejó atrapar. El Mirandés, con más pólvora en las botas y sangre fría en el minuto final, se llevó un botín que le mantiene pegado a la cabeza. Para los de casa, la lección es tan vieja como el fútbol: dos goles de ventaja no bastan si no se cierran los partidos.

articles.title: Mbappe double helps Real Madrid thump Rayo Vallecano 4–1 in La Liga
articles.summary: Goals from Bellingham and Carreras ease pressure on Madrid manager Mourinho after they lost their last league game.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe struck twice to help Real Madrid smash Rayo Vallecano 4-1 and pull level with Barcelona at the top of La Liga.

Jose Mourinho’s side got back to winning ways on Saturday after a defeat by Real Betis in their previous top-flight outing, with a convincing victory against neighbours Rayo.

Jude Bellingham and Alvaro Carreras were also on target for Real Madrid, while Sergio Camello pulled one back for the visitors early in the second half.

Champions Barcelona visit Levante on Sunday, looking to extend their 100 percent start to the campaign and restore their lead over Madrid.

Mourinho’s side took a commanding three-goal lead against Rayo by half-time.

“[It was] fundamental to win, above all after losing the last game in La Liga,” Mourinho said.

“We killed the game in the first half – that’s not easy, working like we did after the Champions League game, not just physically, but mentally.”

Los Blancos took the lead from the penalty spot in the 14th minute after Florian Lejeune clumsily felled Carreras. Mbappe sent Rayo goalkeeper Emil Audero the wrong way.

The French forward helped create the second, after Lejeune gave the ball away under pressure from Vinicius Junior. Carreras exchanged passes with Mbappe and drilled home.

Handed a first start for Madrid, the club’s record signing Yan Diomande cut inside from the right flank with a rapid dribble that left Rayo’s defence scrambling but lashed his shot high and wide.

Bellingham notched Madrid’s third goal and his third of the season after Vinicius charged down the left and cut the ball back for the England international, who has started the season in top form.

Mourinho defended Vinicius in midweek after some Madrid supporters whistled him in the Champions League win over Inter Milan.

Mbappe powered a strike from distance against the post as Madrid sought a fourth, while Pedro Diaz forced a rare save from Thibaut Courtois at the other end, the Belgian with a strong hand to push away his effort.

Diaz hit the post early in the second half as Rayo tried to find a foothold at the Santiago Bernabeu.

Mbappe, who stated his case for why he should win the Ballon d’Or this week, almost added a second with a low drive.

Rayo pulled one back in the 51st minute when Vinicius gave the ball away to Camello under pressure, and the forward poked past Courtois.

It was the Spanish forward’s sixth goal of the campaign, making him joint-top scorer with Barcelona’s Raphinha and Mbappe.

Benat San Jose’s side, 15th, had further chances to score but Courtois pushed out Giorgi Tsitaishvili’s drive and an effort from Lejeune.

Mourinho brought on Turkish midfielder Arda Guler to help regain some control.

“Arda is very good, he’s got a lot of quality, he influences the team’s play in a good way, and today he made a difference in terms of the stability of the game,” said Mourinho.

Guler helped create Madrid’s fourth for Mbappe in stoppage time, lethally finishing low and across goal.

It was Mbappe’s seventh goal of the season across all competitions.

“Conceding the [early] penalty was a blow, then we had another mistake when bringing the ball out,” said Rayo coach San Jose.

“I think we could have scored in the first half too, but it’s true that they were better …

“We have to congratulate Madrid, but I’m proud of the players because the second half was much better.”

On Tuesday, Real Madrid travel to face Elche, while Rayo Vallecano host Espanyol.

articles.title: Keelon Russell, Ryan Coleman-Williams Box Score Stats, Highlights from Alabama Win vs. Kentucky
articles.summary: The Alabama Crimson Tide used a dominant fourth quarter run to pull away for a 45-17 victory over the Kentucky Wildcats on the road, improving to 2-0 on the season.
articles.body:
The Alabama Crimson Tide used a dominant fourth quarter run to pull away for a 45-17 victory over the Kentucky Wildcats on the road, improving to 2-0 on the season.

Alabama entered Saturday's matchup as a 10.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , as Kentucky took the Crimson Tide down to the wire on the road.

Despite early struggles from the Crimson Tide, Keelon Russell and Ryan Coleman-Williams helped Alabama rally from a one-point halftime deficit to secure a dominant 28-point victory.

The young quarterback suffered through a slow start, committing a pick-six and losing a fumble in the opening quarter.

To open their first second quarter possession, the Crimson Tide's first points came off field goals, but the quarterback's nightmare was not yet over. He committed another interception before halftime as Alabama trailed 14-13.

Alabama found its first touchdown on a running play by EJ Cromwell with 3:00 left in the third quarter before Daniel Hill added another touchdown late in the quarter as Alabama began to pull away, leading 31-17.

Russell found his connection in the end zone for the first time at the 9:08 mark of the fourth quarter, finding Rico Scott on a short, 5-yard pass. It would be his lone touchdown pass of the game despite the high-scoring performance by the Tide.

Back in January, ESPN's Matt Miller took a look at Williams' potential draft stock, noting the junior wide receiver's struggles with drops. Williams recorded 18 over his past two seasons. He also saw a dip in production when it came to finding the end zone last season, recording four touchdowns his sophomore season after eight as a freshman.

At just 19 years old, Williams would enter the 2027 NFL Draft as a freshly 20-year-old, making him one of the younger prospects in the class.

In his opening game against the East Carolina Pirates, the 6-foot wide receiver hauled in five receptions for 130 yards without a score. He added four receptions and 43 yards Saturday against Kentucky, highlighting Miller's concerns about his future in the NFL if he is unable to consistently find the end zone.

Meanwhile, sophomore quarterback Russell is not eligible for the NFL Draft until 2028. Despite this, in his first year as the Crimson Tide's go-to under center, he has already become a topic of conversation.

Russell led his team to a 48-10 season-opening win over East Carolina, completing 18-of-30 passes for 256 yards and adding a rushing touchdown. He did not record a passing touchdown in his debut for the team.

After Saturday's win and Russell's struggles with turnovers, the young passer will need to put emphasis on his play in the air moving forward if he wants to see any draft buzz surrounding him.

Despite Alabama scoring a combined 93 points through the first two games of the season, Russell has recorded just one passing touchdown. If he hopes to follow in the footsteps of Alabama's great quarterbacks of the past, he'll need to find more consistency in the passing game.

Alabama will host the Florida State Seminoles next Saturday.

articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “Having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you” - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodman’s shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy
articles.summary: International Sports News: Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion .
articles.body: Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion and, as of January 2026, the highest-paid player in NWSL history. But her childhood looked very different from what many people expected from the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman. Trinity and her brother DJ once lived with their mother, Michelle Moyer, in a Ford Expedition and cheap motels in Newport Beach. Through those difficult years, Michelle kept life feeling normal for her children. That bond helped shape Trinity into the player she is today.How did Trinity Rodman live in a car despite being Dennis Rodman’s daughterHaving a famous father did not mean Trinity Rodman grew up with an easy life. After Dennis Rodman and Michelle Moyer separated, Trinity, her brother DJ and their mother faced serious money problems. For a period, they moved between a Ford Expedition and motels when Michelle could afford a room.The situation was especially strange because they were living in Newport Beach, where Trinity went to a wealthy school. She has spoken about seeing classmates arrive in expensive cars while her own family was trying to work out where they would stay.On Call Her Daddy, Trinity explained just how unusual those years were:“We had a Ford Expedition and we lived in that for a little bit. Mind you, in Newport Beach… So imagine living in a car going to a rich school when everybody else is in Rolls-Royces and Range Rovers. But my mom tried to make every situation seem smoother than it actually was. For me and DJ, it was never embarrassing because we had each other and we had our mom.”For Trinity and DJ, however, those memories were not only painful. Their mother tried hard to make sure they still had happy childhood moments. At motels, they could eat breakfast, use the pool and spend time together before school. That helped the children see their family life differently from how an outsider might have seen it.What did Trinity Rodman say about her relationship with Dennis RodmanTrinity’s relationship with Dennis Rodman has remained one of the most talked-about parts of her story, but it has also been one of the most painful. She has said that her father was often absent while she was growing up and that there were long periods when they had little contact.That distance became impossible to ignore as Trinity began making a name for herself in soccer. Instead of being known only as an athlete, she was repeatedly asked about being Dennis Rodman’s daughter.She later spoke openly about how difficult that connection could feel:“He’s a person. He’s not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else… Hearing his voice is painful because it’s missing him mixed with the fact that he’s an alcoholic. I answer the phone now for my conscience, but it took me a long time to realize that having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you. I had to build everything myself.”Dennis has also publicly admitted that he was not the father he wanted to be. At his Basketball Hall of Fame induction, he said he wished he had been a better father.For Trinity, though, her own career could not depend on her father’s reputation. Her speed, finishing, attacking ability and work on the field became the things that made people remember her.Why does Trinity Rodman call Michelle Moyer her role model?If Dennis Rodman gave Trinity a famous last name, Michelle Moyer gave her the support that helped her grow into a professional athlete. Michelle raised Trinity and DJ largely as a single mother and remained closely involved in Trinity’s soccer journey.The Guardian reported in 2021 that Trinity saw her mother as her main support system. That feeling has remained central to how she talks about her childhood and her success.Trinity put it simply:“My mom wasn’t in the NBA, but she’s my role model. She is my world, my rock, and my right hand. She’s the strongest person I know. People always say, ‘Oh, you get your athleticism from your dad,’ but my work ethic, my heart, my grit, and the woman I am today-that’s 100% my mom.”That is an important part of Trinity’s story because her biggest influence was not another famous athlete. It was the person who was there when money was tight, when the family had nowhere stable to stay and when Trinity was still only a young girl trying to understand her world.How did Trinity Rodman turn a difficult childhood into a soccer careerTrinity’s soccer career moved quickly once she reached the professional level. She entered the NWSL with the Washington Spirit in 2021 and became the youngest player ever selected in the league’s draft at the time. She went on to win the NWSL Rookie of the Year award and helped the Spirit win the league championship that same year.Her rise continued with the U.S. women’s national team. She became an important attacking player for the USWNT and was part of the squad that won Olympic gold at the 2024 Paris Games.The success also changed the way her name was viewed. Instead of being introduced mainly as Dennis Rodman’s daughter, Trinity became a major soccer star in her own right.In January 2026, she reached another major point in her career when she re-signed with the Washington Spirit on a deal worth more than $2 million per year. The agreement made her the highest-paid player in NWSL history.That achievement says a lot about how far she has come. The girl who once went to school after sleeping in a car is now one of the biggest names in American women’s soccer.Why is Trinity Rodman’s story inspiring beyond soccerTrinity Rodman’s story is not simply about becoming famous despite having a difficult childhood. It is about how she chose to define herself.She could have spent her career being introduced through her father’s name. Instead, she has built an identity around her own performances and the people who stood beside her. Her mother remained a constant presence, while soccer gave Trinity a place where her effort could speak for itself.Her journey also explains why the success means more than trophies and contracts. The Olympic gold medal, NWSL championship and record-breaking deal are major achievements, but they came after years of work that had little to do with her father’s fame.Trinity has been clear about that point herself: a famous parent can give someone a name, but it cannot do the training, handle the pressure or play the game for them.For Trinity Rodman, the most important part of her legacy may be that she did not allow her father’s story to become her own. She took the difficult parts of her childhood, held on to the support her mother gave her and built a career that now belongs completely to her.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Arsenal stretch Premier League lead as Liverpool, Chelsea stumble; Bruno Guimaraes stars in Sunderland win
articles.summary: Football News: Arsenal strengthened their grip on top spot in the Premier League on Saturday as defending champions extended their lead to three points after beating.
articles.body: Arsenal strengthened their grip on top spot in the Premier League on Saturday as defending champions extended their lead to three points after beating Sunderland 2-0, while Liverpool and Chelsea both dropped points at home.Arsenal were made to work hard for the victory at the Stadium of Light, but Bruno Guimaraes produced the moment that unlocked the game. The Brazil midfielder, who joined Arsenal from Sunderland's fierce local rivals Newcastle in the summer, came off the bench at half-time and curled a superb long-range effort into the top corner in the 58th minute.His celebration added another layer to an already emotional occasion. After being booed by the home supporters, Guimaraes cupped his ears as he ran towards the corner.“It is a beautiful moment for me and my family,” Guimaraes told TNT Sports. “Everyone knows my amazing history at Newcastle, but now I’m trying to create a new history here. I’ve started on the right foot.”Bukayo Saka then sealed Arsenal's victory from the penalty spot in the seventh minute of added time after Sunderland defender Reinildo Mandava was sent off for bringing down the forward inside the box.Raya saves Arsenal after controversial penaltyArsenal's victory could have taken a very different turn when Sunderland were awarded a penalty. Enzo Le Fee stepped up, but David Raya produced a crucial save.Mikel Arteta was furious with the decision to award Sunderland the spot-kick, which came after Ezri Konsa was adjudged to have held Dan Ballard during a set-piece.“It’s a huge win, but it could have been something very different,” Arteta said. “It’s unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable. This changes the course of the season, the championship, and it’s not acceptable.”The Premier League confirmed the penalty was awarded for holding, but Arteta remained adamant that the decision was wrong.“I’ve been in football for almost 27 years, 28 years. It’s not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league,” he said.Arsenal's victory moved them three points clear at the summit, with Manchester City second ahead of Sunday's derby against Manchester United.Liverpool held as big-money attack misfiresLiverpool missed the chance to keep pace with Arsenal after being held to a goalless draw by Fulham at Anfield.The result was particularly frustrating given the club's huge investment in attack. British-record signing Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Victor Munoz all failed to find a breakthrough against a Fulham side that had entered the match without a clean sheet and without a league point.Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson admitted the home side failed to produce its best football.“Collectively we didn’t play well. Many things we tried to do, we couldn’t do well,” Alisson said.Manager Andoni Iraola was also disappointed after Liverpool's run of back-to-back wins was halted.“When you draw, especially at home, you can’t be happy,” Iraola said. “Today we lacked a bit of freshness and we did not do enough offensively to make the difference.”Chelsea's defensive woes continueChelsea also surrendered points at Stamford Bridge, drawing 2-2 with newly promoted Hull.Morgan Rogers put Chelsea ahead in the seventh minute, but Mohamed Belloumi struck twice to turn the match around before Joao Pedro rescued a point for the hosts with a 66th-minute equaliser.The result extended Chelsea's defensive concerns. Xabi Alonso's side have conceded at least two goals in every Premier League game and 12 across their last six matches in all competitions.“We can do better. We got what we deserved,” Alonso said. “We need to be more solid and be more controlled. New players and new staff. This is the process. In a few months I’m sure we’ll be able to control better.”Elsewhere, Tottenham remained without a Premier League goal after a 0-0 draw with Everton, while Aston Villa's miserable start continued with a 2-1 home defeat to Nottingham Forest. Ipswich beat 10-man Crystal Palace 3-2 through Zian Flemming's 90th-minute winner, while Bournemouth and Brentford played out a 2-2 draw.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Iowa Honors Marching Band Member Derek Phillips With Tribute During Week 2 Game vs. ISU
articles.summary: The Iowa marching band honored member Derek Phillips, who died Tuesday after collapsing during the season-opening game against Northern Illinois, during Saturday's contest against Iowa State.
articles.body:
The Iowa marching band honored member Derek Phillips, who died Tuesday after collapsing during the season-opening game against Northern Illinois, during Saturday's contest against Iowa State.

The Hawkeye Marching Band previously announced that it would honor Phillips "in several ways," including keeping the leader position of the H1 squad empty for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

The band also spelled out his name on the field at halftime and wore black ribbons in his honor. There was a moment of silence at the game as well.

Phillips' family announced on Instagram he suffered "sudden cardiac arrest" during the game. They also said they made the "heartbreaking decision to remove" him from life support.

"Despite the extraordinary efforts of the ICU team at the University of Iowa Hospital, the damage to his brain was too severe, and we have made the heartbreaking decision to remove life support," the family said. "... Derek is comfortable, surrounded by family, and enveloped in the music he loved so much. Thank you for every prayer, every shared experience, and every bit of love you've given to our boy."

In the band's initial statement , it said, "Derek Phillips was our mellophone section leader, a beloved member of the School of Music horn studio, and the kind of friend, student, and musician that represents the very best of what it means to be a Hawkeye."

articles.title: Texas comes back to defeat No. 1 Ohio State: 1 bettor wins $1.2 million wager on Longhorns
articles.summary: One bettor won nearly $1 million on Texas on Saturday night.
articles.body:
No. 1 Ohio State took on Arch Manning and the No. 4-ranked Texas Longhorns in Austin, Texas, on Saturday night as a rare underdog under head coach Ryan Day. OSU looked great for three quarters, building a 23-3 lead. But Texas fought back with 21 unanswered points, including the winning touchdown with 25 seconds left to secure a remarkable 24-23 victory .

The Longhorns' win was quite profitable for one bettor in Las Vegas.

A bettor at Caesars Palace placed a $1.2 million wager on Texas to win at -127 odds before the game, which won nearly $945,000 after the Longhorns completed their huge comeback. Texas had in-game money-line odds of as long as 31-1 at some sportsbooks at one point.

Texas had a turnover on the first play of the game, fell behind 10-0 after the first quarter and trailed 20-3 at halftime. The Longhorns converted multiple fourth-down tries in the fourth quarter to keep touchdown-scoring drives alive and were aided by Ohio State kicker Connor Hawkins missing a 45-yard field goal attempt with 4:16 remaining and Ohio State up 23-17.

The Buckeyes entered as 2.5-point underdogs, which marked the first time in Day's tenure at Ohio State that he was an underdog in a regular season game against any team not named Michigan. Ohio State had gone 1-1 straight-up and against the spread in the two games as an underdog against Michigan.

Texas faces UTSA next week, while Ohio State plays Kent State.

articles.title: Arch Manning Reacts to Texas' Historic 20-Point Comeback, Recalls 'Nightmares' from 2025 OSU Loss
articles.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning gave his thoughts on the No. 5 Longhorns' 24-23 comeback victory over No. 1 Ohio State on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Texas quarterback Arch Manning gave his thoughts on the No. 5 Longhorns' 24-23 comeback victory over No. 1 Ohio State on Saturday night.

"I'm just so proud of our guys, all three phases," Manning told ESPN's Laura Rutledge after the win (h/t ESPN's Pete Thamel ). "It wasn't very pretty, but we found a way to win. That's what good teams do."

Arch, KD dap up after wild Texas comeback win over Ohio State

The Longhorns erased a 20-point deficit before emerging victorious in the fourth quarter.

It marked the first meeting between Texas and Ohio State since Aug. 2025, as the Buckeyes previously won by the final score of 14-7.

"We couldn't lose to them again," Manning said (0:31 mark). "I had nightmares about that game last year. So, I'm glad to get a win tonight."

The Longhorns similarly struggled against the Buckeyes' defense on Saturday, as they were only able to muster three points through three quarters and trailed 23-3 heading into the fourth.

Texas finally started to gain momentum early in the final quarter with a short touchdown pass from Manning to Ryan Wingo.

The Longhorns' defense subsequently forced an Ohio State punt before their offense followed it up with a 13-play, 72-yard drive that ended with a one-yard touchdown run by Hollywood Smothers.

The Buckeyes looked to take a two-score lead on their next possession, but a 45-yard field goal attempt missed.

Texas' offense stayed hot, driving 73 yards down the field before taking their first lead of the game with another short score from Smothers as just under 30 seconds remained in the fourth quarter.

Time expired during Ohio State's last drive, sealing the final result.

Manning went 23-of-37 for 195 yards and one touchdown compared to one interception. He also rushed for 24 yards.

As Manning navigates through his second season as a full-time starter, Texas improved to 2-0 with the statement win.

articles.title: No. 4 Texas scores 21 unanswered in fourth quarter to beat No. 1 Ohio State 24-23
articles.summary: The Longhorns trailed 23-3 at the start of the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
Will Texas be the new No. 1 team in the country?

The No. 4 Longhorns scored 21 straight points in the fourth quarter to get a 24-23 win over No. 1 Ohio State on Saturday night. Hollywood Smothers dove over the pile at the goal line with 25 seconds to go to tie the game ahead of Gianni Spetic's go-ahead extra point.

After trailing by 23-3 early in the fourth quarter, Texas was in front.

Ohio State didn't have any timeouts after Texas' touchdown, and any hope of a miracle game-winning drive ended with a holding penalty on the first play.

"It wasn't very pretty, but we found a way to win," Arch Manning told ABC after the game. "That's what good teams do."

The Buckeyes' loss is the first time since at least 2003 that the No. 1 team in the AP Top 25 led by 17 or more points at halftime and ended up losing the game.

With a defense that clearly started leaking oil in the second half, one question will be on Ohio State fans' minds this week. Should the Buckeyes have let Texas score earlier?

Texas took over with 4:16 to go after a missed 45-yard field goal by Ohio State's Connor Hawkins. Had the kick gone in, Ohio State would have been up two scores.

Instead, Texas embarked on a 12-play drive that went 71 yards. And it took a while to get that final yard. The Longhorns got to the Ohio State 1-yard line with 1:23 to go after a 19-yard completion from Manning to Emmett Mosley V.

At that point, Ohio State had one timeout after using its second before the completion. Should Ryan Day have saved it?

Day elected to take that timeout before second down, after his defense stopped Smothers short of the end zone. After the timeout, there were 51 seconds on the clock.

The Buckeyes then stopped Smothers again on second down, though the play necessitated a replay review. The review confirmed that Smothers didn't get into the end zone. That allowed Texas to take even more time off the clock before snapping the ball on the third-down play Smothers got into the end zone on.

Of course, it was not a guarantee that Texas would have gotten into the end zone. But it was also highly probable. Had Ohio State put up less resistance on first down, the Buckeyes would have had over a minute remaining and a timeout in their pocket for an attempt at a game-winning drive.

On a day where the high hit 100 degrees, Texas ended up running 78 offensive plays. And more than half of them came over the final 21 minutes of the game

The Longhorns ran 40 plays across their final three possessions. And all three of those drives ended in touchdowns.

Texas cut the lead to 13 with a 15-play, 91-yard drive that ended with a TD pass to Ryan Wingo with 14:19 to go. After Ohio State went three-and-out, the Longhorns then ran 13 plays that covered 72 yards before Smothers scored his first touchdown of the game.

The Longhorns also converted fourth downs on each of those first two touchdown drives.

It was quite the contrast from Texas' first two drives of the games. Smothers fumbled on the first offensive play of the game after taking a swing pass from Manning. After Ohio State kicked a field goal, Manning had Cam Coleman wide open for a deep completion.

But the pass was just too far ahead of Coleman, who had to dive to make the catch. As Coleman brought the ball into his body, it bounced out of his grasp when he hit the ground and flew into the air for a Jaylen McClain interception .

Manning finished the game 23-of-37 passing for 196 yards and a TD along with the interception. After the run game was stuffed for most of the evening, Smothers ended up with 21 carries for 74 yards and two scores, while Raleek Brown had 10 carries for 54 yards.

Had Ohio State hung on for what looked like a convincing win in the third quarter, Jeremiah Smith's play would have been the takeaway. The star junior wide receiver had eight catches for 164 yards and a touchdown that put the Buckeyes up 17 with just 10 seconds to go before halftime.

As Ohio State's offense slowed down in the second half, Smith's production did too. Ohio State had just five first downs over the final 30 minutes of the game and ran 28 plays to Texas' 47 in the final half.

Ohio State QB Julian Sayin was 17-of-32 passing for 278 yards, a TD and an interception. No other Buckeyes player than Smith had more than four catches or 37 receiving yards.

articles.title: Ohio State is 1-3 in its last four games, and Ryan Day needs to provide some answers — fast
articles.summary: The Buckeyes suffered a stunning defeat after leading 23-3 against Texas. It is Ohio State’s third loss in its last four games, and the head coach needs to t...
articles.body:
There really isn't much to be said about what happened to Ohio State on Saturday night.

The Buckeyes dominated in the first half against Texas, holding a 20-3 lead at the half and extending that to a 23-3 lead with 8:09 left in the third quarter. The Longhorns proceeded to score touchdowns on three straight possessions as Ohio State sputtered out and collapsed, ultimately losing the game 24-23.

It is among the worst losses of the Ryan Day era, second to only the 13-10 defeat to Michigan in 2024.

There is no shortage of reasons why the Buckeyes lost this game.

Ohio State could muster only three points and 132 total yards in the entire second half. After scoring points on four of their first five drives of the game, the Buckeyes' five possessions in the second half netted three punts and two field goal attempts, the second of which — a 45-yard kick that would've iced the game with 4:21 remaining — wasn't even close.

That said, while not every loss for Ohio State under Day has been this dramatic, almost all of them have featured at least two of three key elements: shortcomings in the red zone, poor clock management and a disastrous special teams unit.

Texas was practically begging Ohio State to run away with it early on, gifting the Buckeyes a red zone trip right from their opening possession after a fumble. The resulting drive netted 11 yards on six plays, and Day's group ended up with a 26-yard field goal.

That was a central theme of the game. Ohio State only managed 13 points on its first four trips to the red zone, with another 30-yard field goal and a turnover on downs at the Texas 12-yard line thrown in the mix.

It was not dissimilar to the 2016 loss to Clemson in the College Football Playoff, where the Buckeyes' red zone woes ultimately turned a potential blowout into a heartbreaking loss.

Then came the poor clock management. Once Texas got the ball to the Ohio State 1-yard line with 1:23 left to play, Day should have called his final timeout and allowed the Longhorns to score, giving Julian Sayin and the offense more than a minute to try and put together a drive to win the game only needing a field goal.

Instead, the Buckeyes made Texas run three more plays to reach the end zone, leaving Ohio State with 25 seconds left, zero timeouts and zero chance of any last-minute heroics.

It isn't the first time poor clock management has aided in an Ohio State loss under Day, as a bungling of the final possession against Georgia in the 2022 College Football Playoff saw the Buckeyes get the ball back with 51 seconds left before mustering only a 50-yard field goal attempt, which they obviously missed, with three seconds remaining.

Which brings me to the final point: special teams.

Ohio State's special teams has been a complete and utter disaster throughout Day's tenure in Columbus.

A missed field goal played a factor in that Georgia loss, a missed chip-shot led to a loss against Indiana in last year's Big Ten title game, and another missed kick against Miami in the College Football Playoff could've changed the tenor of that contest — just to name a few!

Even when they went out a got a 'proven' kicker, it still didn't work out. Connor Hawkins missed a potential game-sealing 45-yard field goal with 4:21 remaining. The kick would've made a comeback nearly impossible at 26-17, but instead Texas was given the chance to take snatch victory from the jaws of defeat, and they did.

It hasn't only been field goals, though. Punting has also been objectively horrible.

Joe McGuire ranked 109th in FBS in punting a year ago, and Ohio State had no issue trotting him back out there for this season. After averaging 41 yards per punt against Ball State — a mark that would have tied for 113th nationally in 2025 — he averaged 39 yards per punt against Texas.

The Buckeyes' inability to flip the field didn't lose them the game against the Longhorns, but it certainly didn't help! It is inexcusable for a place like Ohio State to not be able to go out and get at least a replacement-level punter.

It may seem like a small thing, but when talent equates in games of this magnitude you simply have to win on the margins. Day clearly does not understand that this also applies to the special teams unit, and it continues to burn him in these big games no matter how many losses they take.

The Buckeyes have lost three of their last four games, and while they will have a few tune-up opportunities coming up before their next big matchup against Indiana on Oct. 17, why should we really expect anything to change?

Day's teams continue to lose the same types of games in the same types of ways, and he has yet to learn from any of them. The offense turtles when times get tough, the defense has trouble getting stops late, the special teams unit is completely ineffective and the time management is nonsensical.

The head coach is going to have to take a look in the mirror and figure out a real, material fix to some of these problems, or we are going to see a few similar results come October and November.

articles.title: What Josh Heupel saw from QB Faizon Brandon vs Georgia Tech for Tennessee football
articles.summary: Josh Heupel praised Faizon Brandon's play in Tennessee football's win over Georgia Tech on Sept. 12, even though his stats were unimpressive.
articles.body:
ATLANTA − Tennessee football quarterback Faizon Brandon faced some adversity while playing on the road for the first time in his very young college career.

Furman offered little resistance in his first career start but Brandon was challenged in Week 2 at Georgia Tech . His first road start didn't look pretty in the final box score but it was more than enough to get the No. 18 Vols (2-0) to a 45-24 win over the Yellow Jackets (0-2) on Sept. 12 at Bobby Dodd Stadium.

"The stat sheet's not going to be elite. I actually really like how he played the game," UT coach Josh Heupel said. "I thought he was composed, he handled himself in situational football pretty well. First game on the road, 18 years old, handled himself well."

Tennessee football vs Georgia Tech: See our best photos of Vols, Faizon Brandon

Brandon completed 10 of 21 passes for 148 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. He was sacked once and added 23 yards on five rushing attempts.

He was particularly inaccurate in the first half, completing only 5 of 15 passes but racking up 106 yards and two touchdown passes. Of his five first-half completions, four went for 15 yards or more and three gained 20 yards or more.

Those strong throws helped the Vols regain control after falling behind 10-7 first quarter on a blocked punt returned for a touchdown. And, with the help of a more efficient running game in the second half, Brandon completed five of six second-half passes for 42 yards.

The Vols ripped off 24 unanswered points in the second and third quarters before cruising behind 299 team rushing yards. And while the numbers weren't as stellar as they were against Furman, Heupel was pleased with Brandon's poise.

"There were a couple things that he's going to learn from and get better from. All in all, really good," Heupel said. "He had a great look, demeanor. He's been pretty consistent with that."

articles.title: La hora de Jonathan David
articles.standfirst: El canadiense se enfrenta a la oportunidad de dar el paso hacia adelante que lo catapulte como el 9 del Atlético
articles.summary: El canadiense se enfrenta a la oportunidad de dar el paso hacia adelante que lo catapulte como el 9 del Atlético
articles.body: Aunque su incorporación sobre la bocina durante el último día del mercado de fichajes venía justificada por la necesidad de complementar a Julián Alvarez y Sorloth, los problemas musculares que padece el argentino y la lesión que ha impedido al noruego estrenarse en esta temporada empujan a Jonathan David a dar el paso adelante que lo catapulte como el 9 del Atlético con carácter de urgencia. Así, después de que Lookman, Baena y Kang-in Lee hicieran las veces de delantero durante las primeras jornadas, al canadiense le llega la hora de acelerar su integración y tratar de justificar su fichaje. Una empresa que pasa por emular sus cinco temporadas en el Lille, en las que se hizo un nombre en Europa tras anotar 109 goles (además de repartir 31 asistencias) en 232 encuentros. De ahí que tras dilatarse su debut en Bilbao al sufrir unos problemas cervicales y estrenarse con la camiseta del Atlético en Anfield con 18 minutos en los que se mostró intrascendente, Jonathan David se ve obligado ahora a aumentar sus prestaciones. En este sentido, tras someterse a un plan individualizado para alcanzar el tono físico de sus compañeros y tras someterse a un trabajo extra después de varias sesiones con el fin de afinar su puntería y ensayar sus movimientos como delantero de referencia, el canadiense ya está listo para enfrentarse a la prueba de fuego de sostener el ataque rojiblanco. Empezando por el partido de esta noche en Anoeta, pues independientemente de que salga de inicio o desde el banquillo, la responsabilidad goleadora empieza a recaer sobre sus espaldas. Ni más ni menos que como sucedió durante su visita al Metropolitano de hace dos campañas, cuando firmó el doblete con el que el Lille acabó de remontar el gol inicial de Julián Alvarez.

articles.title: Hamza, a la sombra del mejor Raphinha
articles.standfirst: El ariete estrenará hoy renovación, a la espera de minutos ante el gran momento del brasileño
articles.summary: El ariete estrenará hoy renovación, a la espera de minutos ante el gran momento del brasileño
articles.body: Hamza Abdelkarim estrenará esta tarde en el Ciutat de València su nuevo acuerdo con el Barcelona, después de que el pasado viernes alcanzara una entente con el club para ampliar su contrato hasta 2030. El delantero egipcio, una de las grandes sensaciones de la pretemporada azulgrana, afronta, sin embargo, un escenario exigente en este inicio de curso. Raphinha está a un gran nivel como falso nueve y no admite rotación. Hamza, pese a ser un delantero centro puro, ha visto cómo, de momento, se le cerraban las puertas del equipo por el excelente rendimiento del brasileño. El egipcio apenas ha disputado cuatro minutos en competición oficial, contra el Rayo Vallecano. Pero el internacional, que terminó la pretemporada como el máximo goleador de la plantilla, no se rinde y espera que su momento pueda llegar hoy contra el Levante. Además, Hansi Flick volverá a recurrir a las rotaciones esta tarde. Es una nueva oportunidad para que Hamza pueda sumar minutos. El técnico alemán, precisamente, elogió ayer su renovación porque entiende que el internacional aporta un perfil único en la plantilla: es un delantero centro de referencia, con presencia en el área y características diferentes a las de otros atacantes del bloque azulgrana. La renovación de Hamza hasta 2030 confirma la apuesta del Barcelona por un futbolista al que considera una pieza importante de cara al futuro, pero el egipcio no quiere limitarse a esperar. Su objetivo es irrumpir cuanto antes en el presente culé y aprovechar cada oportunidad que le conceda Hansi Flick, como hizo en verano. Hamza, eso sí, ha entrado en todas las convocatorias del Barcelona y continúa esperando su momento. La competencia es especialmente dura porque Raphinha atraviesa un momento extraordinario. El brasileño ha marcado en todos los encuentros disputados hasta ahora, tanto en LaLiga como en la Champions, y ya suma ocho goles: seis en la competición regular y dos en el máximo torneo continental. Además, el Levante puede convertirse en una víctima inédita para Raphinha. El brasileño se ha enfrentado en dos ocasiones al conjunto granota y en ambas ganó, aunque todavía no ha conseguido marcarle. Esta tarde tendrá una nueva oportunidad de ampliar sus registros y mantener una racha goleadora que, por ahora, está marcando el inicio de temporada. Hamza, con su renovación recién firmada, busca que ese futuro empiece a convertirse también en presente. Hoy podría volver a tener minutos.

articles.title: Texas football: Arch Manning, Longhorns shock No. 1 Ohio State behind a historic comeback
articles.summary: Texas overcame a handful of early mistakes in a 24-23 win over No. 1 Ohio State at Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns entered the fourth quarter trailing...
articles.body:
On Saturday night, Texas football made history against Ohio State .

Texas overcame a handful of early mistakes in a 24-23 win over No. 1 Ohio State at Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns entered the fourth quarter trailing by a 23-3 score, but three touchdowns helped Texas complete an improbable comebacker Hollywood Smothers ' 1-yard with 25 seconds left and Gianni Spetic 's subsequent extra points sealed the win.

The 20-point comeback was tied for the fourth-largest in school history. Texas also ralled out a 20-point hole in a 35-34 win over TCU in 1954.

Now 2-0, Texas will return to Royal-Memorial Stadium next week for a home game against UTSA (2-0).

Massive mistakes lead to halftime deficit for Longhorns

On Saturday, Texas stumbled out of the gates. On the game's first snap, Texas running back Raleek Brown fumbled away the football at the end of a backfield reception.

How bad was that start? Over the first 69 games of Steve Sarkisian's Texas tenure, the Longhorns had averaged 8.7 yards over their first offensive snaps. Texas had gotten touchdowns on two first plays – Xavier Worthy scored on a 75-yard reception against Oklahoma in 2021 and Ryan Wingo matched that highlight against Vanderbilt last year – but none of those inaugural offensive plays had featured a turnover.

Brown's fumble led to a short field goal for Ohio State, and things didn't get any better for Texas. An interception that bounced off the hands of a diving Cam Coleman ended the next UT possession and set up a touchdown drive for Ohio State. Texas finally got on the scoreboard with Gianni Spetic's second-quarter field goal, but that 37-yard kick came six plays after Ryan Wingo dropped a 30-yard touchdown pass.

Down 10-3 after Spetic's kick, Texas allowed 10 points to be scored in the first half's final two minutes. The Buckeyes' last seven points – which were tallied on a 19-yard touchdown catch by Jeremiah Smith with 10 seconds left – was the byproduct of a botched last-minute drive by the Longhorns. With UT trying to cut into the Ohio State lead, Brown caught a nine-yard pass on a 3rd-and-10 play but stepped out of bounds before picking up the first down. After keeping its offense on the field for fourth down at Ohio State's 41-yard line, Texas faked a simple handoff, got gimmicky and lost yardage when Wingo was run down in the backfield.

Forty-nine seconds later, Ohio State was heading into halftime with a 20-3 lead.

Down by 20, Texas completes its comeback

While facing its largest halftime deficit since it trailed Georgia by 23 points in 2024, Texas fell further behind in the third quarter as Ohio State kicked a 48-yard field goal. The Longhorns, however, made things interesting in the final frame.

Texas opened the fourth quarter with two scoring drives as Manning found Wingo for a 3-yard score and running back Hollywood Smothers scored from one yard out. That Smothers score made it a 23-17 game with 7:14 left.

Ohio State had a chance to end UT's hopes of a comeback on its next drive, but Connor Hawkins missed a 45-yard field goal. Given the football with 4:16 left, Texas quickly marched the football into Ohio State territory. Texas got with football within a few inches of the goal line before Smothers leaped over the pile to secure the victory.

Ohio State was given a few last-second shots at a response but did not get the football past its 25-yard line as Texas secured its first win over the No. 1 team in the AP poll since it beat Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl in 2008.

Ohio State and Texas played on Saturday in front of the third-largest crowd in school history. This marked just the fourth time in school history that the Longhorns had hosted the No. 1 team in the Associated Press' poll. The Longhorns are now 2-2 in those games.
