articles.title: How we grade Auburn football against Southern Miss: Report card
articles.summary: How did Auburn football fare against Southern Miss? Here's our grades for offense, defense and special teams, as well as our MVP.
articles.body:
AUBURN — After narrowly surviving its season opener with a win, Auburn football left no doubt in its next contest, beating Southern Miss 43-8 on Saturday, Sept. 12, in its home opener at Jordan-Hare Stadium .

Coach Alex Golesh's squad scored on the first play of the contest and ran up the score with relative ease, handling its Group of 5 foe to remain undefeated at 2-0. USM fell to 1-1.

Here's our report card for Auburn 's performance, including grades for all three units, coaching and our game MVP.

Did Auburn do more than enough to impose its offense on a Group of 5 foe? But it still had one turnover, and 7 of its 10 penalties went against that side of the ball. It wasn't stellar on third downs either, but going 4 for 5 on fourth downs was a high point.

Hard to find much to complain about here. Multiple turnovers, backfield stops and an opponent held to pedestrian rates all around.

Alex McPherson's career-long field goal before the half was the high point, but Auburn was able to find some success in the return game, and punter Hudson Kaak only had to use his leg twice.

Perhaps the whistles are a group effort, but 10 penalties in any game is far from ideal. However, Auburn's offense got out of its shell. Golesh put more of his playbook on display, and Auburn executed.

There were a slew of stellar individual performance against Southern Miss, but Jordan's two-interception day was notable. He set the tone, and he doubled his career picks after 31 games.

It wasn't perfect, but few performances are. Auburn made some strides after a shaky season opener, and it's an A all in all.

articles.title: Ohio State’s 24-23 loss to Texas is the worst non-Michigan defeat of Ryan Day’s tenure
articles.summary: This loss had all of the worst hallmarks of the Ryan Day Experience and is the worst non-Michigan loss of his Ohio State tenure.
articles.body:
I've been through a lot of ups and downs in my 45 years as an Ohio State fan, but tonight's 24-23 loss to No. 4 Texas is going to be one of the toughest pills to swallow. In the first 30 minutes of the top-five matchup in Austin, everything went the way of the No. 1 Buckeyes. Balls bounced their way; every offensive decision paid dividends; the defense was nasty; the Scarlet and Gray were playing with a near-feral aggression that seemed perfectly suited for their road, underdog status. They came out swinging and landed punch after punch after punch.

But then after halftime, something changed. The punches went from haymakers and uppercuts to crosses, then to jabs, then to slaps, then to nothing more than flailing whiffs unable to connect.

Some of that can be blamed on the oppressive Texas heat taking its toll as the game went on; more can be blamed on how the Longhorns never gave up and continued to fight; and, unfortunately, I think even more can be blamed on the Ohio State coaching staff doing what we have seen far too often during the Ryan Day era outside of the four-game run in the 2025 College Football Playoff National Championship: they took their foot off the gas and coached not to lose rather than to win.

The team's four consecutive losses to Michigan are in their own category, separate from everything else, but aside from those rivalry losses, this is, by far, the worst defeat of Ryan Day's tenure as Buckeye head coach.

The embarrassing loss to Missouri in the 2023 Cotton Bowl was demoralizing and wholly unacceptable, but it was a meaningless postseason exhibition in which a number of key players opted out. This was a marquee, primetime matchup against a fellow blueblood with major College Football Playoff implications, and OSU was up 20-3 at halftime before essentially deciding to play a completely different brand of football after the break than the one that netted them a three-score lead to begin with.

In the first two quarters, there was an energy and electricity to everything Ohio State did. It still wasn't perfect — the Buckeyes continued to struggle in the offensive red zone — but it felt like there was a plan and an aggression that not only played to the strengths of the Buckeyes' deep and talented roster, but also kept Texas and especially quarterback Arch Manning off-balance.

Before the game, I wrote about how the circumstances of this game allowed Ryan Day to coach with an aggression and freedom , if he chose to go that direction. If he had done that from start to finish, even if they did end up losing, at least they could hang their hats on having played in a way that gave them the best chance to win and made the most of their talent. And, for the first half, that is exactly how it felt.

But instead of going out and completing the middle-8 win, Ohio State punted after halftime and essentially took its boot off the Longhorns' neck. Texas deserves plenty of credit for what happened from there; the Longhorns adjusted, Arch Manning settled in, and a very good team refused to let the game get away from them.

But that is exactly the reason that Ohio State's response was so frustrating. Rather than countering those adjustments with more aggression and creativity, the Buckeyes seemed to retreat from the very approach that had put them in control in the first place.

Even after a quiet opening to the second half, Ohio State still led 23-3 entering the fourth quarter. From there, the collapse was entirely avoidable.

This game was another painful microcosm of the Ryan Day experience at Ohio State. This wasn't solely about conservative play-calling; this loss exposed the entire collection of recurring problems that seem to surface when Day's teams get conservative — less defensive pressure, less offensive creativity, more red-zone failures, more settling for field goals, etc.

Tonight, OSU only mustered 13 points on four trips into the red zone, couldn't get off the field on third and fourth down, missed a likely game-winning field goal, refused to rush more than three — occasionally four — on defense, and completely abandoned any and all creativity on both sides of the ball.

Connor Hawkins' missed field goal isn't on Day's temperament, but repeatedly settling for field goals and creating situations in which one kick could essentially determine the outcome of the game absolutely is. Allowing Manning to convert multiple fourth-quarter fourth downs isn't on Day, but the defense not being schemed to put an erratic quarterback under pressure in high-leverage moments certainly is.

This game had all the tedious, painful hallmarks of the worst of Ryan Day's tendencies.

In the 12-team playoff era, a single loss — especially to a top-five opponent — clearly doesn't ruin your season. Ohio State still has plenty of opportunities to build its résumé and work its way into the College Football Playoff.

That is why I could have lived with a loss had the Buckeyes maintained the aggression, creativity, and effort that made the first half so exciting. If Texas had simply fought back and beaten Ohio State while the Buckeyes continued throwing punches, so be it.

But when you can almost literally see a switch being flipped between the best version of the Buckeyes and a version instead made in the image and likeness of their naturally timid and anxious coach , it becomes insultingly predictable.

And that is what makes this loss so maddening. OSU has more than enough talent to beat any team in the country, but they seem incapable of maintaining the level of execution (from both players and coaches) necessary to make the most of that talent.

Up 23-3 with just over 23 minutes left in regulation should never result in a loss for Ohio State. There is too much skill on the roster, too much experience on the coaching staff, and too much at stake for the Buckeyes to let a game like this slip away.

What makes this loss most aggravating, though, is that Ohio State showed that they knew exactly how to beat Texas. For 30 minutes, the Buckeyes were aggressive, creative, physical, and fearless. They dictated the game and forced a confused Texas team to react. They played like a team with nothing to lose, and that philosophy produced a three-score lead on the road in a hostile environment against one of the best teams in the country.

Then they stopped doing every last bit of that.

That is the part Ryan Day has to answer for. Texas deserves credit for fighting back, but Ohio State simply cannot continue to give up leads because its staff starts coaching as though protecting the lead is more important than extending it. The Buckeyes didn't need to reinvent anything in the second half in order to finish out the win. They simply needed to adjust to what Texas was doing and keep playing the brand of football that had put the Longhorns in a blender in the first place.

Instead of going all-in, the Buckeyes folded back into the cautious, anxious version of themselves that Day has all too often allowed to surface in the biggest games. This should have been a signature win. Instead, it became the worst non-rivalry loss of Day's Ohio State tenure, not because the Buckeyes never had an answer for Texas, but because they proved they knew the answer and then chose to stop using it.

articles.title: Why you should sit Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker in fantasy football Week 1
articles.summary: Here's why Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is a must-sit your fantasy football lineup for Week 1
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is expected to make his first Chiefs start this week against the Denver Broncos on 'Monday Night Football.'

Fresh off Super Bowl MVP honors, Walker comes into the 2026 season with high expectations. Kansas City signed the 25-year-old running back this offseason in an effort to alleviate some pressure on quarterback Patrick Mahomes , who is still recovering from last season's brutal knee injury.

Walker will aim for a fast start as he plays in front of the crowd at Arrowhead Stadium for the first time.

Why you need to sit RB Kenneth Walker III in Week 1 vs Broncos

Despite the fact that Walker currently occupies the flex spot in my starting lineup, I don't have a great feeling about his ability to produce on Monday. Though I do expect the former Seattle Seahawk to have another impressive season, he will likely struggle against the Broncos. Denver had the second-best run defense in the league last year and will do everything it can to force the Chiefs' offense into a one-dimensional attack. I think Walker will be serviceable at best against the Broncos.

RB Kenneth Walker vs Broncos stat predictions in Week 1

Walker could very easily have a monster game on Monday. Denver finished the 2025 season with one of the league's top defenses, but that doesn't guarantee they will repeat their success. If Walker can find early opportunities, he just might carry his team to victory. That being said, I don't see the reigning Super Bowl MVP having a highly productive game this week. The Broncos are out for blood and will pull out all the stops to take down the Chiefs at Arrowhead.

I expect Walker to rush for fewer than 75 yards and score one touchdown at most.

articles.title: Leo Messi, Sam Surridge shine in Supporters' Shield slugfest
articles.summary: By Ben WrightMIAMI – MLS Matchday 26's Walmart Saturday Showdown between Inter Miami CF and Nashville SC was billed as an instant classic. It did not disappo...
articles.body:
MIAMI – MLS Matchday 26's Walmart Saturday Showdown between Inter Miami CF and Nashville SC was billed as an instant classic. It did not disappoint.

The reigning MLS Cup presented by Audi champions and current Supporters' Shield leaders played to a thrilling 2-2 draw , with Lionel Messi and Sam Surridge taking center stage at Nu Stadium.

The Argentine No. 10's legendary left foot delivered the second of Miami's goals that were bookended by a Surridge brace, including the 91st-minute equalizer.

"This was a big boys' game tonight," Nashville head coach B.J. Callaghan told reporters postmatch. "Two really good teams going toe to toe."

Saturday's result maintained Nashville's nine-point lead over Miami on top of the East Conference, while keeping them eight points clear of Vancouver Whitecaps FC in the Shield race, with nine matches left to play.

It also helped the Coyotes reinforce their recent dominance of the Herons. After eliminating Miami in the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup Round of 16, Nashville produced a statement 4-1 blowout victory at GEODIS Park last month in MLS action.

"I thought the game had a lot of intensity, a lot of physicality, some high-level play," said Callaghan.

Unsurprisingly, Messi had a major part to play on the night.

The back-to-back Landon Donovan MLS MVP scored a brilliant first-time curler in the 62nd minute, retaking sole possession of the MLS Golden Boot presented by Audi lead over FC Dallas star Petar Musa with 19g/13a on the season.

"God gave him this gift," interim manager Guillermo Hoyos said of Messi's latest masterpiece. "... He's a one-of-a-kind player, he's one of a kind. He cannot be repeated."

However, Surridge had the last word at Nu Stadium.

After giving Nashville a fourth-minute lead, the Designated Player striker came to the rescue in second-half stoppage time, poking home the last-gasp equalizer off a Dayne St. Clair rebound.

With the brace, Surridge improved to 15g/1a while helping the Coyotes take one step further towards the Shield.

articles.title: 5 things we learned about Ohio State in its loss to Texas Saturday
articles.summary: Ohio State allowed Texas to roar back with 21 unanswered points in the second half. Here are five things we think we learned in defeat Saturday.
articles.body:
Ohio State was up and in control of what would have been a massive win for its College Football Playoff résumé, but then the game plan turned into a grinding of gears instead of the team popping the clutch and continuing to go out on the open road and run away into the night.

The result? The Texas Longhorns scored 21 unanswered points to enjoy what they will no doubt consider an epic comeback. Buckeye fans will think the opposite, and for good reason. A game profile that should never go in the loss column did just that because of some curious decisions and gameplay in the second half.

After each game, we like to look back and see what kind of lessons we might have learned about Ohio State, and things tend to be a little more negative after a loss, but that's life in the big city.

Here are five things we think we learned after Ohio State's collapse in the Texas night.

Even the coaches Ohio State pays handsomely still make bad decisions

Ohio State's coaching staff has a ton of experience, and even at the NFL level. They are getting paid an awful lot to make in-game decisions, but that was a big problem today. We, of course, don't know how much head coach Ryan Day's fingerprints are on some of these things, but the offense buttoned things up, the defense played soft-shell coverage with only three down linemen most of the time in the second half, and then there's the end of the game.

It would have been a goal-line stand for the ages, the way Ohio State was giving up yards through the middle of the defense in the running game at the end. Texas was inside the two-yard line, yet the Buckeyes used their last two timeouts, allowed precious time to tick off the clock, and the Longhorns still scored (of course). You have to play the percentages there and let Texas score, get the ball back with two timeouts and over a minute left to try and get in field goal range. There are some questions that need answering on multiple fronts.

Jeremiah Smith is indeed human (sort of) for Ohio State

To be fair, Jeremiah Smith isn't the reason Ohio State lost. In fact, he finished with one whale of a game. However, with the game on the line, he couldn't corral two passes he normally would, and it was in winning time. As a result, the Buckeyes had to punt the ball instead of hanging on and continuing a drive that would have perhaps resulted in a score to seal this game.

Again, he's still the best player in college football, and he put the cape on multiple times tonight. He just picked a bad time to run into Crypton with the game on the line, according to some. It probably won't happen again, and he might just be the reason this team makes special memories still. But yeah, even the best have their humble pie in rare situations. Even if the catches weren't the easiest.

Connor Hawkins looked a lot like Ohio State kickers of the recent past

A loss like this has a lot of blame to go around, and Connor Hawkins will likely be one of the main scapegoats. Many Ohio State fans had to be triggered when Hawkins hooked the potential 45-yard game-winning field goal wide left. It would have sealed Texas' fate despite all the second-half mishaps, but instead, somewhere, Jayden Fielding is nodding in empathy.

Hawkins was brought in to solidify these pressure kicks that have etched their memory in Buckeye Nation's minds, but now, at least so far, he's added to it. I get it. These are pressure-packed situations, and it isn't easy, but Hawkins has to be that steadying wind when things are swirling in chaos, and that didn't happen tonight.

The Ohio State defense is not as strong on the defensive line

First of all, what was the deal with all of the three-man fronts in the second half? All that did was let Arch Manning find running lanes (where was the spy), let him sit back in the pocket and go through his progressions, and let him gain his footing and confidence.

Still, the defensive line gave up way too many yards between the tackles and didn't get enough push into the backfield to make Manning see ghosts. The lack of a pass rush up front and inability to be strong up the middle isn't going to be an issue against teams like Ball State and Kent State, but it absolutely will be an issue against the more physical teams like tonight's opponent.

Everything is still on the table, but the margin of error is thin

This loss doesn't take Ohio State out of the College Football Playoff, but it does mean the Buckeyes can't afford to kick themselves in the shins much more. Two total losses probably still get OSU into all the fun, and this isn't a Big Ten game, so there's no hurt in the race for the conference crown, but the schedule is far from easy on the way out.

The Buckeyes still have to go to Indiana, USC , and Iowa , and have to host Oregon and Michigan . Ohio State might have to win four of those games to be safe, and that's before we even look at some games that will end up being closer than we think. The Ohio State coaching staff can ill-afford to let another game like this one get away the rest of the year. However, not all is lost.

articles.title: Watch: Texas football RB Hollywood Smothers' late TD seals comeback over Ohio State
articles.summary: Texas Longhorns fans stormed the field in the thousands after a crazy comeback against Ohio State on Sept. 12, 2026 at DKR in Austin.
articles.body:
New Texas football running back Hollywood Smothers didn't have the biggest game Saturday against Ohio State . No career highs, no 100-yard day for the former North Carolina State star. His longest rush was just 11 yards.

But when UT needed him most, he went above (the Buckeye defense) and beyond (the goal line) to finish off a furious 20-point comeback by the Longhorns. Smothers' second touchdown of the night, with less than 20 second remaining, put Texas ahead for a 24-23 win over the top-ranked team in the country.

He finished the day with 21 carries for 74 yards. He also caught three passes for 29 yards.

articles.title: Week 2 overreactions: Ohio State in trouble, Oregon, Oklahoma out of CFP, Ole Miss will beat Lane!
articles.summary: Week 2 delivered on many fronts and spawned many takes.
articles.body:
When No. 1 Ohio State led No. 4 Texas 23-3 heading into the fourth quarter at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, the overreactions were already pre-written.

Steve Sarkisian can't win the big game. Arch Manning is a flop. Jeremiah Smith for Heisman.

Week 2 gave us what Week 1 could not provide – some dramatic over-reactions that flipped the script on the College Football Playoff race. Who had Michigan and Texas winning instead of No. 11 Oklahoma and Ohio State entering the day?

Sarkisian won a huge game. He's now 4-7 against top-five teams with Texas, but this was the heavyweight victory against a top-ranked team that should propel the Longhorns into the SEC portion of the schedule possibly with a No. 1 ranking. The Buckeyes, meanwhile, lost in shocking fashion by blowing a three-score lead. Manning – who finished 23 of 37 for 196 yards, a TD and an interception – overshadowed Smith – who had eight catches for 164 yards and a TD.

Texas is back. Yes. We can finally say that with a full chest. What were the other over-reactions from Week 2?

No. This loss will sting in Columbus knowing the degree of difficulty left on the schedule for the Buckeyes in the Big Ten. Ohio State coach Ryan Day is now 1-5 as an underdog, and the Longhorns scored on three drives that covered 93, 73 and 73 yards, respectively, as part of the Manning-inspired comeback.

Remember, Ohio State lost 32-31 at No. 1 Oregon on Oct. 12, 2024 before losing 13-10 to Michigan. The Buckeyes still won the national title.

The loss to the Longhorns still is shocking, to say the least. Smith was phenomenal, but quarterback Julian Sayin had an uneven performance. He finished 17 of 32 for 278 yards, a TD and an interception. Defensive coordinator Matt Patricia's defense finally got dinged in the fourth quarter, and the Buckeyes still have a brutal Big Ten schedule that includes trips to No. 21 Iowa No. 5 Indiana and No. 14 USC before November dates with No. 6 Oregon and Michigan. We still think Ohio State can go 4-1 in that stretch, but would a 9-3 team be left out of the CFP?

Day might not want to ask Sarkisian how that scenario can go.

Ole Miss will ruin Lane Kiffin's return with LSU!

No. So, we're going to do Week 3 with No. 8 LSU and No. 9 Ole Miss next week. The Lane Kiffin-Pete Golding coaching matchup will be the constant topic of conversation ahead. Who has the advantage? LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt had three first-half interceptions and the Tigers led Louisiana Tech 10-7 at halftime. It wasn't that close, however. The Bulldogs had just 140 total yards, and LSU still rolled up 528 total yards. Leavitt finished 25 of 38 for 344 yards and a TD and added 22 rushing yards and three more TDs.

Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss finished 23 of 26 for 225 yards and two TDs in a 41-9 victory against Charlotte. There will be drama – and the scene will top what we witnessed in Austin on Saturday. Yet it's tough to pick against LSU in this spot in what could be the most-watched game this September. We're going to stick with Kiffin and the Tigers here.

Oregon will miss the College Football Playoff!

Yes. We'll volunteer this for Freezing Cold Takes if wrong – but the Ducks are having trouble adjusting to losing coordinators Will Stein to Kentucky and Tosh Lupoi to Cal.

Start with the defense, which returned seniors A'Mauri Washington and Matayo Uiagalelei and added Minnesota safety Koi Perich. The all-in factor was there. Oregon had one tackle for loss and allowed 554 total yards to Oklahoma State. The Cowboys gained 368 against Tulsa.

What about the offense? Dante Moore – who finished 14 of 29 yards, with 191 yards and two TDs – was seen trying to fire up teammates on the sideline. Oregon went 0 for 3 on fourth down – and now is 0 for 5 on the season. It's back-to-back lackluster performances, and they still have to play at No. 14 USC (Sept. 26) and No. 1 Ohio State (Nov. 7). Will Oregon split those games based on what we've seen? There is no margin for error.

Oklahoma is out of the College Football Playoff!

Yes. We'll go there, too. Consider the equations in the Sooner State right now.

Oklahoma State lost to Tulsa, then beat No. 6 Oregon. Oklahoma lost to Michigan, who should have lost to Western Michigan. So, do we need to see the Broncos face the Golden Hurricane next?

The Sooners looked bad against the Wolverines in a 17-10 loss. John Mateer, who finished 17 of 33 for 189 yards, a TD and a costly interception to Jyaire Hill in the fourth quarter. Oklahoma is now 5-4 on the road since joining the SEC, and the next matchup on a brutal road schedule is at No. 2 Georgia on Sept. 26. What if the Sooners are a three-loss team after the Red River Rivalry against No. 3 Texas?

We do like the Oklahoma defense – which allowed just 263 total yards — but the victory against Michigan is what pushed Oklahoma into the CFP last season. Defensive back Reggie Powers III leads that nasty defense, but that will only take you so far.

Look out for Virginia Tech, UNC in the ACC!

No. But we're monitoring Virginia Tech closely.

The Hokies lost to Old Dominion 45-26 last season. On Saturday, Virginia Tech won 44-21 to improve to 2-0 under James Franklin. Ethan Grunkemeyer finished 31 of 42 for 327 yards and two TDs in a high-volume passing attack, but the Hokies managed just 2.1 yards per carry. Virginia Tech plays at Maryland and Boston College the next two weeks – so a 4-0 start and a top-25 ranking heading into the Oct. 2 matchup with Pittsburgh is in the cards.

North Carolina beat East Tennessee State 35-3, which means Bill Belichick has the Tar Heels at 2-0 heading into the matchup at Clemson in Week 3. The Tigers beat North Carolina 38-10 last season – so we'll see how far that progress goes. We like the defense so far. Defensive tackle Xavier Watts has four sacks in two games, and quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. hit 15 of 20 passes for 244 yards and two TDs.

No. 19 Washington beat Utah State 16-14 in a squeaker. The Huskies average just 3.8 yards per carry the last two weeks, which needs to improve in Week 3 against Eastern Washington.

Florida is 2-0 for the first time since 2021 after a 52-3 win against Campbell. The Gators might be ranked under first-year coach Jon Sumrall. Running back Jadan Baugh has 296 rushing yards on 11.9 yards per carry and five TDs.

Marty Whims II was the guest offensive coordinator for Akron for one drive against Robert Morris. The four-play drive went for 23 yards but was derailed by a false start and a fumble . Hey, Nick Saban told Whims to stay ahead of the sticks and run the ball. Does Whims want that first-down pass play back?

articles.title: Why we just saw the biggest win in DKR history, and other Texas vs Ohio State observations
articles.summary: As bad as things looked for three quarters, Texas and QB Arch Manning gave us a comeback of all comebacks over No. 1 Ohio State. These were our staff takes.
articles.body:
Down 23-3 in the fourth quarter. Twenty-one unanswered points - against the No. 1 team in the country. A Heisman Trophy campaign that roared back to life. The return of Texas football 's running game, redemption for a quarterback and a program, and a huge win over the Buckeyes that has Texas in place to possibly become the new No. 1 team in the country.

Saturday night's 24-23 thriller had it all.

As bad as Texas' start was, as bad as things looked at halftime and the third quarter, as unlucky and plodding as the Longhorns looked, all that turned around in the fourth quarter. After surviving what was probably the worst first quarter of the Steve Sarkisian era, No. 4 Texas produced perhaps the biggest win ever at Royal-Memorial Stadium.

Here are some observations we saw from Saturday's win:

Arch Manning etches his name into Texas football history

Texas entered the fourth quarter trailing by 20 points, but pulled off the biggest comeback in program history . Manning has secured his spot in Longhorns lore after ending the game with just 196 yards passing but calmly executing a fourth-quarter rally. It was the third fourth-quarter comeback with Texas trailing in his career.

It also was the biggest comeback in Sarkisian's career, too.

For the night, Manning was 23 of 37 for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He completed 62% of his passes.

Comeback win could key Texas' run to No. 1

Texas has the talent. Now, the Longhorns showed their toughness. It's the type of win that can key a run to the College Football Playoff. And it will certainly get Texas some first-place votes in Monday's poll. The Longhorns never panicked, to the credit of Sarkisian and his team.

Who's No. 1? Here's how the top five teams fared Saturday:

No. 1 Ohio State lost to No. 4 Texas 24-23

No. 2 Georgia beat Western Kentucky 70-20

Jeremiah Smith looks like the best receiver in the game

Give former Texas defensive coordinator Pete Kwiatkowski credit: His units had some issues, but he knew how to slow down Ohio State All-American Jeremiah Smith. New defensive coordinator Will Muschamp couldn't figure it out; after Smith totaled seven catches for 46 yards in two previous games against Texas, he exploded for 164 yards and a touchdown on eight catches Saturday.

While Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo struggled with drops, Smith proved himself the best receiver on the field.

7 p.m. next Saturday at Royal-Memorial Stadium. It's an SEC Network+ game.
